scope: 对一个无解释样板的知识地图节点完成课程标准、统计教育指南、政府教学活动与统计教育研究论文核查；后续获授权施工已完成对应解释初稿，本研究记录不修改源节点或关系。

rules: 先核对来源 description、全部 evidence、assessmentPrompt、ageRange、standards 与真实前后关系。
以预期数据变异为统计问题判定核心；不得用“是否涉及群体”“是否需要调查”或“是否为数字答案”替代定义。
明确总体、观测单位、变量与情境；区分总体和实际样本。
数值变量与类别变量都可能产生统计变异；单一摘要值仍概括一组可能不同的数据。
课程标准、教学活动和研究论文分别记录其证据性质与限制，不将课程目标冒充因果效果研究。
外部来源核查完成不等于解释起草、独立数学教研或儿童理解验收完成；taxonomy hasResearch=false 保持原值。

sourceCatalog.title: CCSS 6.SP.A.1 — Statistical Questions
sourceCatalog.supports: Defines a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in related data and accounts for it in the answer; contrasts an individual's age with students' ages.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Defines the target standard, not an instructional-effect study.

sourceCatalog.title: Pre-K–12 Guidelines for Assessment and Instruction in Statistics Education II (GAISE II)
sourceCatalog.supports: Requires an investigative question to specify the intended population and variable and anticipate variability; explains that a single summary value can represent a distribution of varying values.
sourceCatalog.limitation: A professional guideline synthesizing research and expert judgment, not a single causal experiment.

sourceCatalog.title: U.S. Census Bureau — What is a Statistical Question?
sourceCatalog.supports: Grade 6 activity asks students to distinguish statistical and non-statistical questions, formulate questions, collect data and draw conclusions.
sourceCatalog.limitation: Describes activity goals and design, not an independent impact evaluation.

sourceCatalog.title: Arnold & Franklin — What Makes a Good Statistical Question?
sourceCatalog.supports: Distinguishes investigative questions from questions used in other stages of statistical problem solving and discusses criteria for good statistical questions.
sourceCatalog.limitation: A conceptual/research discussion, not direct validation of this project's lesson.

sourceCatalog.title: Illustrative Mathematics — Identifying Statistical Questions
sourceCatalog.supports: Provides grade 6 examples and non-examples, including days in March, dogs' ages and the proportion of students who like watermelons.
sourceCatalog.limitation: A curriculum task and teacher commentary, not an independent empirical study.

records.title: 提出统计问题
records.alignment: CCSS 6.SP.A.1 directly matches the node's distinction between questions anticipating variable data and questions with one fixed answer. GAISE II adds precision about population, variable and variability.
records.research: The CCSS standard provides the direct learning target. GAISE II specifies population, variable and expected variability. The Census Bureau's Grade 6 activity offers a matching identify/formulate/answer sequence. Arnold and Franklin clarify that investigative questions are one part of a broader statistical questioning process; this node should stay focused on formulating the initial question. Illustrative Mathematics provides suitable counterexamples.
coverageAudit: Classify all four source examples and justify each by expected variability.
For a statistical question, name population, variable and expected variation; explain why a typical single-number summary still represents varying values.
Explain why a group-count question can be non-statistical and rewrite a personal journey question as a group statistical question.
records.revision: No explanation sample created in this research pass. Defined the content boundaries and acceptance evidence for a later draft.
records.remaining: Explanation drafting, independent mathematics/teaching review and child comprehension testing remain pending.
